Apple explicitly identified **five reported results** as unfavorably affected by currency weakness against the U.S. dollar in fiscal 2024 versus fiscal 2023:

| Reported result | Currency weakness cited | FY2024 vs. FY2023 reported result |
|---|---|---|
| **Greater China net sales** | Renminbi | $66.952 billion vs. $72.559 billion, down 8% |
| **Japan net sales** | Yen | $25.052 billion vs. $24.257 billion, up 3% |
| **Rest of Asia Pacific net sales** | Foreign currencies, collectively | $30.658 billion vs. $29.615 billion, up 4% |
| **Products gross margin** | Foreign currencies | $109.633 billion vs. $108.803 billion |
| **Products gross margin percentage** | Foreign currencies | 37.2% vs. 36.5% |

For the three regional net-sales results, Apple described an unfavorable year-over-year currency impact. For both Products margin measures, currency weakness and a different product mix **partially offset the benefit of cost savings**. Thus, an unfavorable currency impact did not necessarily mean the reported result declined.

**Sources:** Apple fiscal 2024 Form 10-K, “Segment Operating Performance,” printed p. 22 (PDF p. 25), and “Gross Margin,” printed p. 24 (PDF p. 27).
